title: Base change of fibrewise dense smooth charts and strict laws
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. An open $U\subset Y$ in an $S$-scheme is $S$-dense if $U_s$ is dense in $Y_s$ for every $s\in S$. An $S$-rational map is a morphism on an $S$-dense open, modulo agreement on an $S$-dense common open; an $S$-birational map is represented by an isomorphism between $S$-dense opens. Smoothness and finite type have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A strict birational law on a smooth separated finite-type $S$-scheme $Y$ with nonempty fibres is an associative $S$-rational map $m:Y\times_SY\dashrightarrow Y$ for which there are opens $D,V,W\subset Y\times_SY$, each dense in every fibre of both projections to $Y$, such that $m$ is defined on $D$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(x,m(x,y))$, $(x,y)\mapsto(m(x,y),y)$ induce isomorphisms $D\simeq V$ and $D\simeq W$, respectively. If $f:Y\to S$ is smooth and $U\subset Y$ is $S$-dense, then for every $T\to S$ the open $U_T\subset Y_T$ is $T$-dense. If $Y$ is smooth, separated, of finite type and has nonempty fibres, these properties also hold for $Y_T\to T$. If $m$ is a strict birational law on $Y$, its base change is a strict birational law on $Y_T$; the base changes $D_T,V_T,W_T$ witness strictness. These statements hold for arbitrary $T\to S$, including the projections from iterated fibre products of a covering base.

proof.text: First verify the density assertion in the slightly greater generality of any morphism $Z\to B$ with a fibrewise dense open $H$. For $b'\in B'$ over $b\in B$, the fibre after base change is $Z_b\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b')$, and its open is the inverse image of $H_b$. Apply [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open] with field $\kappa(b)$, scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b')$, and base scheme $Z_b$: the projection $\pi$ to $Z_b$ is open. If $O$ is any nonempty open in this new fibre, $\pi(O)$ is a nonempty open of $Z_b$, hence meets $H_b$. A point in that intersection has a preimage in $O$, which therefore meets $\pi^{-1}(H_b)$. This proves density. The fibre identifications follow by comparing projections in the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-base-change]. In particular it proves the claimed assertion for $U\subset Y$. No smoothness, finiteness, or irreducibility is needed for this topological argument.

source.place: Tag 0383, lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open; the nonempty-open argument expands BLR 2.5, printed p.55

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change] to the smooth morphism $Y\to S$; it gives smoothness of $Y_T\to T$ without requiring properness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and clause (2) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] to obtain separatedness and finite type. Nonempty fibres say exactly that $Y\to S$ is surjective. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] gives surjectivity of $Y_T\to T$, hence nonempty fibres: a point $y'$ over $t$ gives $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y')\to (Y_T)_t$ by the fibre-product universal property. This also covers $T=\varnothing$, when the fibre assertion is vacuous.

An open immersion remains an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Base change of a representative $h:H\to Z$ of an $S$-rational map is therefore a morphism $h_T:H_T\to Z_T$ on an open domain, which is $T$-dense by step 1. If two representatives agree on an $S$-dense common open $E$, their base changes agree on $E_T$, again $T$-dense by step 1; thus the operation is independent of representatives. For an isomorphism of dense opens, base change of its inverse is an inverse, because their composites have the same projections as the identity. The same universal-property argument shows that base change preserves composition and the product projections. This constructs the base-changed rational map $m_T$ from $m:D\to Y$ and identifies $(Y\times_SY)_T$ with $Y_T\times_TY_T$.

source.place: BLR 2.5, printed p.55, definitions and base-change paragraph; expanded using Schemes Tag 01JY, lemma-base-change-immersion

proof.text: Put $P=Y\times_SY$ and fix either projection $p_i:P\to Y$. The projection $p_{i,T}:Y_T\times_TY_T\to Y_T$ is its base change along $Y_T\to Y$: the identification $P\times_{Y,p_i}Y_T\simeq P\times_ST$ is obtained by retaining the two $Y$-coordinates and the $T$-coordinate, with the inverse supplied by those same projections. Each of $D,V,W$ is fibrewise dense for $p_i$ by strictness. Apply the general density argument of step 1 with $B=Y$, $B'=Y_T$, and $H$ successively $D,V,W$. Their base changes are therefore dense in every fibre of $p_{i,T}$. Doing this for $i=1,2$ proves all six required fibrewise-density assertions, including fibres over points of $Y_T$ with arbitrary residue-field extensions.

source.place: BLR 5.2 Definition 1, printed p.115; base-change preparation of BLR 2.5, printed p.55

proof.text: Let $\Phi:D\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ and $\Psi:D\xrightarrow{\sim}W$ be the strict-law charts. Base-change their maps and their inverses. The equations $\Phi^{-1}\Phi=\mathrm{id}$ and $\Phi\Phi^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$, and the corresponding equations for $\Psi$, remain equations after base change by step 3. Hence $\Phi_T:D_T\simeq V_T$ and $\Psi_T:D_T\simeq W_T$. To identify them with the required translations, compare their two projections: $\Phi_T$ has projections $p_{1,T}$ and $m_T|_{D_T}$, and $\Psi_T$ has projections $m_T|_{D_T}$ and $p_{2,T}$. The universal property of the product gives exactly $(x,y)\mapsto(x,m_T(x,y))$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(m_T(x,y),y)$. Together with step 4 these are the strictness witnesses.

source.place: BLR 5.2 Definition 1, printed p.115, universal translations and their isomorphism charts

proof.text: Associativity of the given rational law provides an $S$-dense common open $A\subset Y\times_SY\times_SY$ on which both iterated products are defined and equal. Under the canonical identification of its base change with $Y_T\times_TY_T\times_TY_T$, the open $A_T$ is $T$-dense by step 1. The two iterates of $m_T$ there are the base changes of the two original iterates, because product maps and composition commute with base change as checked in step 3. Pulling back their equality proves associativity as $T$-rational maps. For the BLR formulation that the two iterates agree wherever both are defined, use the chosen representative on $D$: its common domain is the intersection of the inverse images of $D$ specifying the two inner and two outer products. Finite intersections and these inverse images commute with base change by their fibre-product universal properties. Its two ordinary morphisms are equal by original associativity, so their base changes are equal on that entire common domain as well. Steps 2--5 now give every condition of a strict birational law on $Y_T$. Every step allowed arbitrary $T\to S$, so it also applies to each projection from any iterated fibre product of a covering base.
